clue.text: Regains consciousness being set adrift in lake

indicators.note: in tells us the rearranged letters go inside the name of the lake

parts.note: Como is the famous lake in northern Italy

indicators.note: something set adrift drifts about loose, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wakes up to find themselves floating loose on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regains consciousness' is a phrasal verb, so the definition fits the two-word answer. Lake Como is in northern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to is the phrasal verb for recovering one's senses after fainting.

clue.text: Resort to monkey business when in clubs and, initially, discos

indicators.note: when in says the monkey and business pieces sit inside the club and disco letters

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

indicators.note: initially says to take only the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: to ape is to monkey, mimicking someone
CO is the short form of company, a business

explanation.surface: A holiday spot where people get up to mischief in nightclubs and discos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monkey business' looks like one phrase, mischief, but splits into two pieces. CAPE COD is a holiday peninsula in Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Cod is a well-known American seaside holiday destination, a resort area.

clue.text: Soaks got up in the morning and demolished retsina

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the letters climb, so the abbreviation is read from bottom to top

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

indicators.note: a demolished thing is broken up and rebuilt anew, so the letters of the Greek wine are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone rose early and polished off the Greek wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' reverses AM to MA, as this is a down clue; 'demolished' rearranges RETSINA into RINATES.
explanation.definitionFit: To marinate food is to steep it in a liquid, so marinates and soaks are synonyms.

clue.text: Heads of some uncooked shark here in Japan

definitions.text: Heads of some uncooked shark here in Japan

indicators.note: the heads of words are their opening letters, so take the first letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: Raw fish such as shark is a delicacy in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of 'some uncooked shark here in' spell the answer, and the whole clue also describes the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is the Japanese dish of vinegared rice often topped with raw fish.

clue.text: I left sign out for crude workers?

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order and rearranged

parts.note: an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a placard as a gesture to rough labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges I, L and OMEN. 'crude' looks like 'rough', but here it is crude oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilmen work in the petroleum industry, extracting crude oil.

clue.text: Arrange a place to sleep around discussions

indicators.note: around turns the whole run of words before it back to front

parts.note: to set things is to arrange them
a bed is a place to sleep

explanation.surface: Someone is told to fix up somewhere to sleep nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses the whole three-word run, not just the bed; 'Arrange' looks like the anagram signal but is a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Debates are formal arguments or discussions on a subject.

clue.text: Forthright journalist charged

parts.note: a forthright person is direct and frank
ED, short for editor, stands for a journalist

explanation.surface: A frank reporter has been prosecuted.
explanation.definitionFit: To be charged with doing something is to be instructed or ordered to do it.

clue.text: Beautiful girl holding a gun is game!

indicators.note: holding means the first piece wraps around the next ones

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful girl or woman
gat is old American slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A pretty woman carrying a pistol is up for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like an adjective meaning willing; it is the definition, a noun. GAT is gangster slang from the Gatling gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a table game in which balls are struck towards holes guarded by pins.

clue.text: Being short of ice cream, seventeens play together

definitions.note: a cross-reference: the plural of the answer at 17 across, performers of notes, all playing at once

indicators.note: short of means the end of the ice cream's name is cut away

parts.note: tutti-frutti is an ice cream studded with candied fruit

explanation.surface: Lacking any ice cream, a group of teenagers amuse themselves together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seventeens' looks like teenagers but points to the answer at 17 across, in the plural; 'short of' cuts the fruity half off the ice cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is the Italian score direction telling the whole orchestra to perform at once.

clue.text: Odds on famous racehorse will exhibit vivacity

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the first piece on top of the second

parts.note: SP, the starting price, is the betting odds on a horse when a race begins
Arkle was a celebrated Irish steeplechaser of the 1960s

explanation.surface: Betting on a legendary racehorse will show a lively spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: SP is the starting price in British horse racing; ARKLE won three Cheltenham Gold Cups (a top British steeplechase).
explanation.definitionFit: Sparkle as a noun means liveliness and brilliance of personality.

clue.text: Soldiers look about for protection from the elements

parts.note: paras are paratroopers, soldiers

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the short word is read backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Troops scan around for some shelter from the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses LO to OL.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a sunshade, shielding a person from the sun.

clue.text: Change target to a race on the river

indicators.note: Change tells us to alter the order of the letters in the word target that follows it

explanation.surface: An instruction to swap a target for something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word between the rearranged word and the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a boating event of rowing or sailing contests.

clue.text: Kind of eccentric playing from sting

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of the words before it are toyed with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Some odd person is performing on stage, apparently derived from a bee's sting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges KIND OF ECCENTRIC. 'sting' is slang for a swindle, not a wasp's jab.
explanation.definitionFit: A sting is slang for an elaborate swindle that cons a victim.

clue.text: Notice man going back to court carrying drug

indicators.note: going back means the name is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: Ted is a man's name
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A man returns to a courtroom with illegal drugs on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a noun, a sign; here it is the verb to spot. E for ecstasy is standard crossword slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice something is to spot or perceive it.

clue.text: Old rock star Joe's entertaining the Spanish birds

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the first piece holds the second inside

parts.note: Joe Cocker was the gravel-voiced English rock singer, giving Cocker's
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: The veteran singer is putting on a show for some Spanish fans.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Cocker was the English singer best known for 'With a Little Help from My Friends'; the possessive gives the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockerels are young male chickens, which are birds.

clue.text: Slippery character with information about soldier returning in woman's underwear

indicators.note: returning means the whole assembled run is read backwards
about means the first piece goes around the soldier

parts.note: an eel is a slippery creature, and a slippery person
GI is an American soldier
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A shifty type with inside knowledge about a soldier is found in women's lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the whole assembled run around, so the pieces appear backwards in the grid; 'about' places the soldier inside the slippery creature first.
explanation.definitionFit: A negligee is a woman's light, often sheer, nightgown or dressing gown worn as nightwear.

clue.text: Fictional king, known for his fondness, of course

definitions.text: Fictional king, known for his fondness, of course

parts.words: Fictional king, known for his fondness, of course
parts.note: a king from Rabelais famed for gluttony: 'fondness, of course' reads as a fondness for courses at the table

explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like 'naturally'; it hints at courses of a meal. Rabelais's giant king had an enormous appetite.
explanation.definitionFit: Gargantua is the giant prince, later king, of Rabelais's satire, renowned for his huge appetite.

clue.text: Too unpleasant — like the guy in the spaghetti movies?

definitions.meaning: too horrible to be spoken of or named

definitions.text: like the guy in the spaghetti movies?
definitions.meaning: Clint Eastwood's Man with No Name in Sergio Leone's Italian-made westerns had no name

explanation.definitionFit: Nameless means unspeakably bad, and also lacking a name, as was Eastwood's cowboy in the spaghetti westerns.

clue.text: Notes player studying the score sheet?

definitions.text: Notes player studying the score sheet?

parts.words: Notes player studying the score sheet?
parts.note: someone who plays notes and reads music: the score sheet looks like a game's tally but is a page of written music

explanation.walkthrough: 'score sheet' suggests a scorer at a game; here it is sheet music.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer of music plays notes and reads from printed scores.

clue.text: Slaughterer he may be — but he avoids gore!

definitions.text: Slaughterer he may be — but he avoids gore!

parts.words: Slaughterer he may be — but he avoids gore!
parts.note: a bullfighter kills the bull yet must dodge being gored by its horns; gore suggests blood

explanation.walkthrough: 'gore' looks like bloodshed, which a killer can hardly avoid; it means being pierced by a horn.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter who kills the bull in the ring.

clue.text: Some offer rickshaws made of iron

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A trader offers rickshaws built from iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals that the letters are found running through 'offer rickshaws'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferric is the chemistry adjective for iron, from Latin ferrum.

clue.text: Cigar's revolutionary source

parts.note: Che Guevara was the famous Argentine-Cuban revolutionary
a root is a source or origin

explanation.surface: A question of where a cigar's radical beginnings lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cigar's' means 'Cigar is'; Che Guevara is fittingly pictured with a cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot is a cigar with both ends cut square.

clue.text: The way out, say, on ship

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
re means on or concerning
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: The exit, for instance, aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is an exit or a means of leaving.

clue.text: Paradoxically two runners are bound to win this

definitions.text: Paradoxically two runners are bound to win this

parts.words: Paradoxically two runners are bound to win this
parts.note: a pair of competitors tied together at the leg: 'bound to win' reads as certain to win but means tied up to win

explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'certain'; here it means tied together. Two people share one prize.
explanation.definitionFit: In this sports-day event two runners have adjacent legs tied together and race as a pair.

clue.text: Guys fondle topless stripper at the front

indicators.note: topless means the top letter, the first, is removed

parts.note: to grope is to fondle

indicators.note: at the front says to take only the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Men paw at a semi-naked stripper by the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' drops G from GROPE, and 'at the front' gives S from 'stripper'. 'Guys' looks like men; here it means guy ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: Guys are the ropes that steady a tent or mast, so they are ropes.

clue.text: Cheerless medical practitioner's spike

parts.note: DR is short for doctor, a medical practitioner
an ear is the spike of grain at the top of a cereal stalk

explanation.surface: A gloomy doctor's sharp point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spike' means an ear of corn, a meaning many solvers miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic word meaning dismal or gloomy.

clue.text: Parking allowed in Scottish river now it's empty

indicators.note: in puts the parking and allowed letters inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, flowing through Aberdeen
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Parking is permitted beside a Scottish river that has now dried up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'now it's' only links to the definition, which is the verb 'empty', not the adjective. The River Dee flows through Aberdeen.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete a supply is to use it up or drain it.

clue.text: Choose the centre of Verona — it's to do with power!

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters, here the pair in the middle

explanation.surface: Picking the middle of an Italian city because of its energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the centre of' takes RO, the middle two letters of VERONA.
explanation.definitionFit: Electro- is a prefix relating to electricity, the power supply.

clue.text: Stands up to cruel sisters

indicators.note: cruel suggests the letters are treated harshly and twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl defies her unkind siblings, as in Cinderella.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cruel' rearranges SISTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist something is to oppose or withstand it.

clue.text: Man crawling taverns

indicators.note: a pub crawl moves from bar to bar, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A fellow doing a pub crawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crawling' rearranges TAVERNS. 'Man' is the verb 'staff', or a manservant, rather than any male.
explanation.definitionFit: A manservant is a male domestic worker, so a man in this sense is a servant.
